answers.answer: Each player takes 12 ordinary turns: 3 in each of four seasons. Courtship rounds have no ordinary turns, service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use.
answers.evidence: Overview: “each player takes twelve ordinary turns”; courtship has “no player turns, service rotation, monument income or Servants’ Hall use.”

answers.answer: Hosting order: rotate service (Quarters→Available, then Expended→Quarters); resolve round event; resolve monument/Servants’ Hall effects; choose and place an activity; invite the exact required gentry; provide required service; resolve positive favours before negative; optionally buy; then send all used servants to Expended, played gentry to personal discard, and return the tile to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading as required. Events and ongoing effects occur before choosing the activity.
answers.evidence: Hosting an activity, steps 1–8; Player Reference: “Host: rotate service → event → ongoing effects …”

answers.answer: Pass order: all servants to Available Service; discard-pile gentry to hand; round event, then ongoing effects; choose £200 or a free Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; then advance the marker if last player. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit.
answers.evidence: Passing: “all servants directly to Available Service → all gentry in your discard to hand → round-track event, then ongoing tile effects → choose £200 or a free Market refresh → optional one tile purchase.”

answers.answer: Yes. The activity and guests are screened using reputation 6.1 at the end of step 2; four Service Help payments may lower actual reputation afterward without invalidating them. Service Help moves a servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service, never directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Reputation screening is “fixed at the end of step 2”; later special actions may lower reputation “without invalidating the activity.” Service Help table specifies Quarters→Available and excludes Expended.

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours; within those groups, choose the order. At minimum reputation, you cannot take a negative reputation favour first to avoid its loss; losses stop at 1.1. A money penalty must be fully payable, using positive money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money as needed; if it cannot be funded, you cannot play that guest/tile.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6; “A money penalty must be fully payable”; “You cannot take a negative favour first to shelter it at minimum reputation.”

answers.answer: Borrow Money costs 2 reputation increments for £100 and is repeatable. Service Help costs 3 increments to move one servant from Quarters to Available and is repeatable. Refresh Market costs 4 increments and is once per turn for that special action. At minimum reputation (1.1) special actions cannot be taken. Service Help cannot take a servant straight from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Special actions table and reputation paragraph: minimum is 1.1 and “cannot … take a special action”; Service Help cannot take directly from Expended.

answers.answer: Host the Butler’s Room with an available butler or underbutler and no gentry. Take up to two eligible servants (not underbutlers) from Servants for Hire into Expended Service, with no fee. Once upgraded, instead recruit one common footman, valet, or lady’s maid from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service; unique servants cannot be recruited.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: “Butler’s Room” paragraph.

answers.answer: A housekeeper may substitute for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With a Brushing Room, a footman may substitute for a valet only when no valets are available. An underbutler may substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, footman), even if that servant type is still available.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: substitution rules.

answers.answer: Acquire an underbutler only by purchasing Butler’s Pantry; it goes immediately to Expended Service. It normally reaches Quarters at your next service rotation and Available Service at your second subsequent rotation; passing or Refresh Service may accelerate availability, and Quarters abilities may help. Opponents cannot recruit it because it is unique, not common.
answers.evidence: “Butler’s Pantry” paragraph.

answers.answer: Pay the Market space price plus the tile’s printed modifier; Reserve base price is £300 plus the modifier. Price cannot be below £100. You cannot acquire a duplicate of a tile you own. Reputation does not restrict purchasing, so you may buy above your reputation.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: “Normally buy one tile…” paragraph.

answers.answer: When a Market space empties, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into rightmost spaces. A drawn duplicate stacks on its matching Market tile and another is drawn. Qualifying Reserve tiles go directly to Reserve and another is drawn. If filling multiple spaces, sort only the newly drawn tiles by sorting number. Buying one tile from a duplicate stack leaves the space occupied, so no refill occurs.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: “Refill” paragraph.

answers.answer: After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar to Reserve; later Service draws go there with that same exception. After courtship 2, also move Market PR1 tiles to Reserve and route later PR1 draws there. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. After each of the first three courtships, a full Market refresh is standard, after Reserve movement.
answers.evidence: “Open Reserve” and “Refresh” paragraphs; Overview confirms full seasonal refresh is standard.

answers.answer: At each ordinary courtship, return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall first. Score the current theme category’s tile VP (including negatives; only current hybrid face counts). Highest score gets one VP card and chooses one Fairchild. On a tie, each tied player draws one VP card and nobody gets a Fairchild. Each player discards one objective; shuffle discards together and bottom-deck them. After courtships 1–3, pass first-player marker anticlockwise (after Reserve opening, Market refresh, and revealing next theme).
answers.evidence: Courtship and seasonal upkeep paragraph.

answers.answer: Final courtship scores all four revealed themes (a repeated category counts twice, including negatives). Highest gets a VP card and Fairchild; tie breaks by reputation level, ignoring wheel position. If still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied winners draw VP cards. Discard the final objective. Then players may use special actions and VP cards for benefits before scoring.
answers.evidence: “Final courtship (round 16)” paragraph.

answers.answer: End scoring includes face-up VP on all improvement tiles; gentry VP in hand and discard; fulfilled remaining objectives; reputation (levels 1–7 score 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28 VP); 2 VP per servant; wealth at 1 VP per £200 rounded down; and retained unused VP cards’ printed VP. Victory ties: final Fairchild holder wins; otherwise highest reputation level; if still tied, share victory. Wheel position does not break ties.
answers.evidence: Final VP table and tie paragraph.

answers.answer: Normally start with five objectives and draw two at round 6; discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three to score. Extra objectives from Main Library or a VP card increase the retained final count without extra discards. Simultaneous courtship discards are shuffled together, then placed face down on the objective deck’s bottom. Tile objectives require ownership, not an upgraded side.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards paragraph.

answers.answer: A VP card may be used immediately when drawn, any time on a later personal turn (multiple cards allowed), and once more after final courtship before scoring. Reveal and discard it for its benefit; used cards go to the bottom of the VP deck. Retained cards score their printed VP; you cannot get both benefit and VP.
answers.evidence: VP card paragraph and benefit table intro.

answers.answer: A normal activity tile must flip to its rose/upgrade side after first use; an already-upgraded normal tile stays upgraded. A hybrid starts underlined-side up and flips after every use, moving to its newly face-up category. A tile that upgrades into a monument (Queen’s or Lionheart Suite) can host only once; it then becomes an ongoing monument whose benefit starts on later turns. Hybrid’s face-up category counts at courtship and for objectives.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: normal tile, hybrids, and monuments paragraphs.

answers.answer: Monuments give one reputation during the ongoing-effects step on hosting turns and passes, never courtship; a newly bought monument starts paying on a later turn. Servants’ Hall works in the same ongoing step (step 2 hosting, step 3 pass): place one available servant there to lose one reputation for an opponent and gain one yourself; that servant goes to Expended at turn end and cannot also serve the activity. Do not target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Monuments and Servants’ Hall paragraphs.

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite: one footman on tile, one casual guest from hand plus normal guest service; doubles all guest favours, including negative; upgrades and remains an activity. Queen’s Suite: housekeeper on tile, one prestige guest from hand plus normal guest service; double one chosen favour only; upgrades into a monument. Lionheart Suite: butler on tile, draw one prestige guest to attend and no personal guest service; doubles nonnegative favours only, keeps guest and discards it at cleanup; upgrades into a monument. All three have a fixed one-guest count that cannot be changed.
answers.evidence: Suite activity table and following fixed-count statement.

answers.answer: Choose a random first player; starting to their left, players choose available family boards clockwise. Bonuses: Asquith adds Dowager Countess; Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gets £300; York gets a footman in Available Service.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 5.

answers.answer: Each player starts at reputation level 1, position 1, with 1/2, 3/4, 5/6, and Max counters stacked (1 showing; Max bottom; no 7/8 counters). Give one each butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid, footman in Available Service; five tiles (Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour, Bowling Green) starter side up; and Lord, Lady, Heir, Young Lady. Only Ponsonby starts with money (£300); Asquith adds a fifth family card, not money.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2–5.

answers.answer: For three players, Servants for Hire gets 3 valets, 3 lady’s maids, 6 footmen, and 2 underbutlers. No butlers or housekeepers. Unused servants returned to the box are unavailable for the game.
answers.evidence: Setup step 6.

answers.answer: Separate starter guests from casual deck, shuffle starters, and deal two to each player; shuffle every undealt starter back into the casual deck. Starter guests are casual guests with a starter icon and otherwise use normal casual rules.
answers.evidence: Setup step 4; Gentry section.

answers.answer: For four players, select five double-sided monuments (one per player plus one). Choose at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze. Tiles that later upgrade into monuments are all placed in the bag and do not count against the selection.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7.

answers.answer: Opening Market fills six different spaces with eligible tiles PR3 or less (including no PR), excluding Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments. Set aside ineligible draws and return them to the bag after filling; stack duplicates in one space. Normal tiles have upgrade icon hidden; hybrids underlined icon showing. Sort by ascending sorting number from the £300 space. PR4 tiles, Servants’ Hall, and double-sided monuments are ineligible.
answers.evidence: Setup step 8.

answers.answer: Put Alderley Hall standard side up, round marker at 1, and one reminder token per player above track. Shuffle theme and VP decks separately; reveal first theme and leave revealed themes in order; place base Charles and Elizabeth Fairchild face up on Alderley Hall. First theme is open, not hidden; earlier themes remain revealed.
answers.evidence: Setup step 9; Overview on open courtship.

answers.answer: At hosting rotation, the servant in Quarters moves to Available Service; the servant in Expended moves to Quarters. Each moves exactly one space. An available servant you do not use remains available.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 1: rotation and unused available servants.

answers.answer: No. Village Fair resolves before choosing the activity, so a Study not already upgraded at that event check earns nothing that turn, even if upgraded later. An already-upgraded Private Study earns £300 and 2 reputation on Village Fair spaces 3 and 9; it is ongoing and need not be hosted again.
answers.evidence: Round-track events table; Private Study paragraph.

answers.answer: Round 6 event resolves on each player’s turn before ongoing effects and activity choice (or before pass benefits in a pass); draw two objectives and keep both secret. Passing players also resolve the event.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure; round-track event table; Passing.

answers.answer: Yes. National Holiday waives PR on all tiles and guests while hosting, so lower-reputation players may play higher-PR ones. All other requirements, including gentry counts/types and service, remain binding.
answers.evidence: Round-track events: National Holiday.

answers.answer: Yes, during Builders’ Holiday you may buy any number from Market and/or Reserve. Complete all purchases at existing prices before sliding/refilling; no special-action or VP-card refresh between purchases. This same unchanged-market restriction applies to Market Purchase VP cards. The summary does not explicitly state whether each tile is charged at its original pre-event price; it says current market prices remain unchanged during the buying sequence.
answers.evidence: Round-track events (any number from Market/Reserve); Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase paragraph (finish purchases before refilling; single unchanged market and no refresh between).

answers.answer: Set all Market tiles aside while drawing replacements; they cannot reappear during that refresh. Leave Reserve unchanged. Refill all six spaces under normal rules, then return the set-aside tiles to the bag and mix.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: “Refresh” paragraph.

answers.answer: Each reputation symbol is one increment. Moving clockwise across position 5→1 raises level; anticlockwise across 1→5 lowers level; a full level spans five increments. Minimum is 1.1 and maximum 7.5 (Max.5); losses below minimum are ignored. At Max.5, excess is lost unless spent immediately on special actions; actions may be taken before or during a reputation favour to make room.
answers.evidence: Reputation, wealth and special actions opening paragraph and Max.5 paragraph.

answers.answer: Money is public; players may not give or receive money between them. Never spend more than you hold. Supply is unlimited (use proxies if needed).
answers.evidence: Money held paragraph.

answers.answer: Ladies can be filled by female family or female guests; casual guest requirements require casual guests and exclude family. Exact printed count is required, with no extra gentry. Family has no PR and needs no personal service (but tile/card requirements still apply).
answers.evidence: Hosting steps 4–5; reputation-screening paragraph.

answers.answer: For an ordinary guest invite, draw the indicated guest, reveal it to everyone, and add it to hand. For screening, draw the stated number, choose the keep number, reveal only kept cards and add them to hand; put rejected cards unrevealed on the bottom of their guest deck.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6; Gentry screening paragraph.

answers.answer: Dismissal is optional, so you need not dismiss anyone. You may dismiss an eligible guest from hand, current activity, or discard, including a guest just drawn earlier during favours. Family can never be dismissed. Put the guest on bottom of its matching deck; it ceases to be yours and will not return on passing or score for you.
answers.evidence: Gentry screening and dismissal paragraph.

answers.answer: Lord: £200 (no choice). Lady: choose screen two casual guests/keep one or optionally dismiss one guest. Heir: choose £100 or one reputation. Asquith Dowager: both £100 and one reputation.
answers.evidence: Base family card table.

answers.answer: The admirer bonus triggers only with a male prestige guest attending, not a male casual guest or female prestige guest. Charles Fairchild is male and prestige, so qualifies. Bonus is two reputation. Young Lady still draws one casual guest in every case.
answers.evidence: Family card table says Young Lady draws one casual and gains two reputation if a male prestige guest attends; Fairchild paragraph identifies Charles as male.

answers.answer: Charles is a prestige guest with no PR, requires a valet, and gives three reputation. Elizabeth is a prestige guest with no PR, requires a lady’s maid, and gives both one prestige guest and two reputation. They are guests, not family cards, so family’s dismissal immunity does not apply to them.
answers.evidence: Gentry and family: Fairchild description; family dismissal rule.

answers.answer: Miss Elizabeth Perkins reduces one opponent by one reputation. Miss Florence Oliver reduces one opponent by two and costs you one reputation. Minimum-reputation protection prevents targeting a player at 1.1.
answers.evidence: Gentry and family: gossip paragraph.

answers.answer: Barn gives one reputation each time you host an Estate activity; owning an Estate tile alone or passing gives none.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: Barn paragraph.

answers.answer: Servants’ Quarters tile can use one servant from Quarters per turn in addition to Available Service; this differs from Service Help, which costs 3 reputation to move a Quarters servant into Available, and ordinary rotation, which moves servants one space. Used Quarters-tile servant goes to Expended Service at turn end.
answers.evidence: Servants’ Quarters tile paragraph; Service Help table.

answers.answer: Private Study’s front side requires two family and a butler; it has no tile favour. It upgrades permanently into an ongoing tile and cannot be hosted repeatedly. The upgraded side gives £300 and 2 reputation only at Village Fair rounds 3 and 9.
answers.evidence: Private Study paragraph; round-track events table.

answers.answer: Unupgraded Main Library: butler plus two family, draw one extra objective. Upgraded: butler plus three family, draw one VP card. Extra objectives increase the retained number scored at the end.
answers.evidence: Main Library paragraph; Objectives and VP cards paragraph.

answers.answer: Objective VP card: draw two objectives, keep one, put the other on the bottom of the objective deck. The kept card is one additional retained objective for final scoring.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table: Objective.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Service VP card moves all servants directly to Available Service and they are usable immediately, including those from Expended Service. Service Help only moves one from Quarters to Available, costs 3 reputation, and cannot take directly from Expended.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table; special actions table.

answers.answer: Hire Servant VP card takes one servant from Servants for Hire (not underbutler) into Expended Service, so it cannot immediately provide service.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table: Hire Servant; Butler’s Pantry paragraph excludes underbutler hiring.

answers.answer: Refresh Guest returns one gentry of choice from your personal discard to your hand, usable immediately. The summary does not specify that it can retrieve family specifically, but gentry includes family; it does not explicitly restrict the returned card from attending the current activity.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table says “one gentry of choice from personal discard to hand; usable immediately”; no explicit family or attendance limitation is stated.

answers.answer: Basic-servant objective counts only common footmen, valets, and lady’s maids, excluding butler, housekeeper, and underbutler. Normal service scoring awards 2 VP for every servant in employ, all types/locations; separate ten-servant objective awards 7 VP for at least ten servants total.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference preface/table; Final VP table.

answers.answer: Monument objective counts monuments, including upgraded Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite. Category objectives count tiles in the specified category, with hybrids counted only in their currently face-up category.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: Monuments; category bonus preface; hybrid paragraph.

answers.answer: Nature Group is 11 VP for Flower Room and any one of English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden, or Garden Maze. Domestic Group is 12 VP for Gabled Conservatory and either Main Library or North Library. Objectives require owning the named tiles at game end, not using or upgrading them.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference table; tile objective paragraph.

answers.answer: Prestige-guest objective counts each prestige guest for 1 VP; every-three-guests objective counts nonfamily guests, awarding 1 VP for each complete set of three. Final Fairchild is a prestige guest and counts. Incomplete groups score nothing.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference guest bonuses and preface that prestige guests include a final Fairchild.

answers.answer: Base reputation objective requires maximum reputation level 7 for 7 VP; wheel position does not matter. Wealth objective gives 10 VP for at least £1200. Ordinary reputation VP is based on level only, and reputation level (not wheel position) breaks ties.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference; Final VP table and tie paragraph; FAQ clarification.

answers.answer: West Terrace both sides require one butler and exactly three family. Unupgraded favour: draw one prestige guest. Upgraded favours: draw one prestige guest and optionally dismiss one to four guests from hand, current activity, or discard to the bottom of matching decks. It remains an activity, not an ongoing dismissal tile.
answers.evidence: Improvements: West Terrace paragraph.

answers.answer: There is no hand or discard-pile limit. Gentry in discard still belong to you and score normally; passing returns them to hand unless dismissed.
answers.evidence: Gentry section: “There is no hand or discard-pile limit”; discard-pile gentry score normally.

answers.answer: You may inspect all Reserve tiles and buy any one, including one beneath another in a stack; no top-only restriction. Every Reserve tile is public.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve paragraph.

answers.answer: You may choose to pass; the player chooses host or pass. If required gentry or service is unavailable, choose another legal activity or pass; if no activity is possible, you must pass.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure; Hosting steps 4–5.

answers.answer: Yes. On a pass you may use the free Market refresh benefit, the once-per-turn paid Refresh Market special action (4 reputation increments), and multiple Market Refresh VP cards in the same turn, each with a separate full refresh, subject to purchase timing. Only the paid special-action refresh is limited to once per turn; free pass and VP refreshes are separate.
answers.evidence: Passing benefit; special-action refresh paragraph: “multiple Market Refresh VP cards”; “once per turn” applies to special-action refresh.
